sources.type: issuer explanatory payment services report for 2024, published on BEAC site in 2026

controls.subject: Critical-service continuity objectives
controls.proposal: Maintain service-specific approved maximum tolerable interruption and maximum admissible data loss; map to ledger, payments, authorization, reconciliation and supporting infrastructure.
controls.evidence: Approved business impact analysis, service-to-asset map, continuity plan and tested RTO/RPO results

controls.subject: Real failover and failback evidence
controls.proposal: Exercise actual critical workload on standby for representative duration and restore primary without financial data loss; compare acknowledged transactions and immutable journals.
controls.evidence: Signed exercise log, timelines, restore checksums, replay ledger, independent reconciliation, exceptions and board/control report

controls.subject: Annual vulnerability and penetration testing
controls.proposal: Track testing coverage of essential/sensitive assets, findings, risk ownership, remediation and reporting; do not equate a scan with an executed penetration test.
controls.evidence: Dated executed test report, scope, findings, board summary and internal control submission

controls.subject: Change/release gate
controls.proposal: Require independent approvals, pre-production test results, controlled migration, rollback and data-restoration rehearsal before changes to financial components.
controls.evidence: Change ticket, reviewer signoffs, release artifact digests, migrations, rollback evidence

controls.subject: Authoritative data dictionary and integrity
controls.proposal: Version business/technical dictionary for money, account, posting, balance, value date, settlement, reversal, status, tenant and external identifiers; reject semantic drift.
controls.evidence: Versioned schema registry, data lineage, invariant/property tests, reconciliation reports

controls.subject: Critical outsourcing continuity
controls.proposal: Map third-party contracts and availability/DR obligations to each critical function; never infer compliance from vendor marketing.
controls.evidence: Signed contract, approved SLAs, provider recovery exercise and institution acceptance

controls.subject: Legal effective vs transition
controls.proposal: Represent 2025-01-01 commencement and 12/18 month transition separately; issuer-hosted narrative 2026 dates are not automatically commencement; require approved legal decision and current amendments.
controls.evidence: Signed current instrument, legal opinion, institution commencement profile and authority record

controls.subject: Electronic payment technical standards
controls.proposal: Create unresolved dependency for authentication, complaints/notifications, dashboards, security, archives and backup; do not implement summary as operative rules.
controls.evidence: Signed original instruction, amendments, scope and institution-specific approval

authority_boundaries.AccountingCore: Only authoritative immutable balanced journals; no DR policy/incident status can mutate posted entries.
authority_boundaries.Recovery: Rehydrate only from verifiable ledger/event history; idempotent replay; quarantined projections until reconciled.
authority_boundaries.RegulatoryCompliance: Owns legal applicability and rule approval; no automatic activation from explanatory reports.
authority_boundaries.InformationSecurity: Owns test/incident evidence, cannot self-certify banking balances.
authority_boundaries.IndependentReconciliation: Signs recovery equality and external settlement proofs separately from operations.

forbidden_transitions: FAILED_OR_UNKNOWN -> PASSED_WITH_EVIDENCE without new independently reviewed exercise

acceptance_scenarios.expected: DR exercise switches to standby but does not execute production failback; mark exercise incomplete.
Actual recovery exceeds approved critical-service maximum interruption or maximum data loss; fail evidence gate and escalate.
A restored journal snapshot is older than durable transaction acknowledgements; reconcile against authoritative append-only events before any restart.
A recovery replay retries a committed payment with the same idempotency key; exactly one authoritative financial posting is permitted.
Standby exercise runs for a trivial non-representative interval; reject evidence of a complete critical-service continuity test.
Cyberattack recovery scenario is omitted from the annual continuity exercise; do not report full Article 34/36 coverage.
Annual penetration test excludes every essential or sensitive service; do not accept a generic perimeter-only report as complete.
Penetration test findings lack remediation evidence, board-level summary or internal-control reporting trace; mark assurance evidence incomplete.
A production release has no pre-deployment functional/security testing or safe rollback and data restoration plan; block deployment.
A dictionary schema change silently changes account-status semantics or monetary field precision; reject until independently reviewed and versioned.
Data transformation rounds, truncates or duplicates journal amounts; reject migration and require exact arithmetic and balancing evidence.
Restored read-model balance differs from the ledger projection; quarantine the read model, preserve authoritative ledger and reconcile.
An outsourced critical service lacks signed recovery and service-level obligations or actual test evidence; reject vendor readiness claim.
A policy engine activates payment authentication or archival requirements based only on the BEAC report's description of Instruction 001/GR/2024; keep policy unapproved pending signed operative text.

blockers: Signed standalone current R-2024/01 and amendment chain
Binding Art 41/Art 30 interpretation and reporting channels
Institution-specific approved BIA, recovery contracts and PCEC mapping
BEAC payment participation, finality and conformance
